cultivar: Local cai cha populations, Fu'an/Fuding/Zhenghe Dabai, and oolong cultivars such as Jinguanyin and Jinmudan in modern lots
processing: Fully oxidised whole-leaf blacks in the gongfu manner: withered, rolled, oxidised, dried and carefully sorted; the Wuyi branch adds pine-smoking (Lapsang) or bud-only picking (Jin Jun Mei).
harvest_season: Spring (April–May) across the province, later at altitude in Zhenghe and Tongmu; autumn lots exist mainly in Fu'an.
appearance_dry: Tight, slim, twisted dark strands with golden tips in varying proportion, from almost all-gold bud teas to tipless Tongmu leaf.
appearance_liquor: Bright red-orange to amber, clear, with a golden ring in tippy grades.
appearance_wet: Even copper-red leaf, small in the north-eastern counties, larger and thicker from Zhenghe.
taste_profile: A family resemblance of honey and caramel sweetness with low harshness, ranging from floral and delicate (Bailin, cultivar Tanyang) to malty (Zhenghe) to longan-and-pine (Tongmu).

brewing.notes: Gaiwan, 88–95 °C depending on the tea (cooler for tippy and floral lots, hotter for Zhenghe and Tongmu), short steeps. Western-style: 3 g per 250 ml, 2.5–3 minutes.

vintage_note: All Fujian blacks are sold by the current year's spring harvest and drunk within one to two years; the exception is smoked and unsmoked Tongmu Xiao Zhong, which is often rested a year and sometimes sold at two to five years old. There is no vintage market for the gongfu teas.
description:
Min Hong is the collective name for Fujian's gongfu black teas, and Fujian is usually named as the place where black tea began. 'Min' is the old name of the province. Strictly the term means three teas of the north and north-east, Tanyang (Fu'an), Bailin (Fuding) and Zhenghe, while tea drinkers often stretch it to the Wuyi teas of Tongmu, from smoked Lapsang souchong to bud-only Jin Jun Mei. Between them they cover the whole range of what Chinese black tea can be, from delicate and honeyed to smoky and dark.

What unites them is the gongfu idea: whole leaf, careful sorting and a drying that aims at sweetness rather than briskness. The local small-leaf bushes and downy Dabai cultivars give honey and caramel rather than tannin. A newer strand uses aromatic oolong cultivars such as Jinguanyin and Jinmudan, and these taste almost floral enough to pass for oolong.

Brewing across the family is similar: a gaiwan, five grams, water a little under the boil and short steeps. But the dial moves: cooler and shorter for tippy Bailin and cultivar Tanyang, hotter for thick-leaved Zhenghe, and near-boiling, no rinse, many steeps for Tongmu teas. None of them wants a five-minute Western steep, which is how most people first meet them and decide Chinese black is thin.

Labels are the trap. 'Gongfu' on a Fujian tea means the style, not a grade; 'zheng shan' and 'Jin Jun Mei' are used far outside Tongmu; and 'Min Hong' itself is sometimes used for blends of whatever the factory had. A good label names the county, the cultivar and the picking standard, and the price should match the claim: genuine Tongmu tea and heavy golden-tip grades are never cheap, while a plain Fu'an spring gongfu is a bargain daily tea.

If you are starting out, buy one of each of the three gongfu teas from the same year and brew them side by side: it is the cheapest education in how cultivar and leaf size shape a black tea.

history:
Min Hong gongfu is the shared name for three Fujian black teas: Tanyang from Fu'an, Bailin from Fuding and Zhenghe from northern Fujian. They have different starting points. Tanyang takes its name from a village at the foot of Baiyun Mountain in Fu'an, with stories starting in the 1851 to 1874 period. Bailin is traced to the 1850s, when Fujian and Cantonese merchants gathered in Fuding to buy and finish black tea. Zhenghe grew into a hub that also finished raw tea from Songxi and Qingyuan in Zhejiang.

Which of the three ranks first is still argued, with Tanyang and Zhenghe both laying claim. No single founding date covers the family, and the name is a grouping rather than a tea you can pick off a bush.
